**At a glance.** 10 molecules × 16 methods = **160 jobs** with def2-TZVP. **You will learn** when error cancellation stops helping, and what dispersion corrections (-D4) and nonlocal correlation (VV10) actually fix.

## Background

![Reactions studied in Experiment 4: Diels–Alder reaction of ethene and butadiene (4a), isomerization of *n*-hexane to neohexane (4b), and formation of the ethane (4c) and methanol (4d) dimers. Carbon is black, oxygen red, hydrogen white; the dotted line is a hydrogen bond.](../images/ex04-reactions.jpeg){fig-alt="Ball-and-stick and line drawings of reactions 4a to 4d" width="500"}

In this experiment you will deal with four more organic reactions commonly found in textbooks:

- **4a**: the Diels–Alder reaction between ethene and butadiene to give cyclohexene, ΔE~ref~ = **–45.40 kcal/mol**.
- **4b**: the isomerization of *n*-hexane to neohexane (2,2-dimethylbutane), ΔE~ref~ = **–2.49 kcal/mol**.
- **4c**: the formation of the ethane dimer, held together only by van der Waals (dispersion) interactions, ΔE~ref~ = **–1.34 kcal/mol**.
- **4d**: the formation of the methanol dimer, held together by a hydrogen bond, ΔE~ref~ = **–5.81 kcal/mol**.

These structures come from the DARC [@goerigk2017; @goerigk2010; @johnson2008] and ADIM6 [@goerigk2017; @grimme2010] subsets of the GMTKN55 database [@goerigk2017], and from the AlkIsomer11 [@curtiss1997; @karton2009] and S66 [@rezac2011; @rezac2011a] subsets of the MGCDB84 database [@mardirossian2017].

As in Experiment 3, use SPW92, BP86, BLYP, PBE, PBE-D4, SCAN, B97M-rV, B3LYP, B3LYP-D4, B3PW91, PBE0, M06-2X, M11, MN15, ωB97M-V and Hartree–Fock (references in [Experiment 3](ex03-organic-a.qmd)), all with the **def2-TZVP** basis set [@weigend2005]. For each functional, compute the reaction energies and the errors with respect to the reference.

::: {.callout-note}
For the dimers (4c, 4d) the reaction is *monomers → dimer*, so a negative ΔE means the dimer is bound. In 4d the two methanol monomers have slightly different geometries (they are cut from the dimer), so compute both.
:::

## Questions

1. Which functional has the most negative error? Which has the most positive?
2. Which functional is the best performer for each reaction? Which is the best overall?
3. Are there functionals that perform badly for these reactions?
4. Compute the wall time divided by the number of SCF cycles for each functional. How do they compare? Compare B3LYP with the other hybrid functionals and with HF.
5. Do the functionals with the **-D4** correction perform better than the corresponding uncorrected ones? For which reactions does it matter most, and why?
